method.actual_lower_mapping: Require stored lower to equal exactly one np.linspace(0,1,401) float; use that point's integer index j.
method.recovery_scope: E1/E4 omitted audit histories. Only states with reported acceptance are replayed through unchanged preprocessing, with saved audit, prediction and score hashes checked. E4 also checks source panel, gold and reference hashes. No PAC call is allowed.

recommended_future_implementation.nominal_integer_gate: Store the selected lower grid index j and sum(z) as Python integers. With q=grid_points-1, compute D=N*(2*j-q)-q*sum(z). Accept only when t<N and D>0.
recommended_future_implementation.conservative_dual_gate: To respect both nominal and actually represented grid values, obtain a,b=float(grid[j]).as_integer_ratio(). Also require D_rep=N*(2*a-b)-b*sum(z)>0. Requiring both is equivalent to exact remainder positivity at min(j/q, represented_grid_value).
recommended_future_implementation.legacy_subset_option: A transition that must never add an acceptance to the frozen floating rule can additionally retain its original float-margin >0 condition; the integer guards then only remove questionable acceptances.
recommended_future_implementation.storage_and_types: Carry j from inversion, not by rounding the bound later. Update an integer gain accumulator from the observed {-1,0,1} gain. Use Python integers, or establish overflow bounds for fixed-width integers. Do not quantize arbitrary [0,1] observations to this lattice.
recommended_future_implementation.outward_rounding_alternative: Use verified interval or directed-rounding arithmetic for every operation in the final remainder expression and require the interval's lower endpoint >0. A single nextafter on the final rounded answer is insufficient to bound all earlier rounding errors.
recommended_future_implementation.scope: These guards fix the final remainder arithmetic and its nominal-grid boundary. They do not certify floating-point stake, conditional-null mean, log-capital accumulation, impossible-null tolerance, or threshold rejection. No general floating-point theorem is asserted.

limitations: This audit addresses only actually accepted groups in the completed frozen checkpoints; it does not replace the statistical guarantee or prove accuracy of every numerical operation.
E1/E4 accepted histories are recovered, not directly stored; saved-hash agreement and deterministic frozen code identify the recovered trajectories.
The exact nominal margin is conditional on the observed selected grid index. Rejection decisions are checked for exact replay, not independently proven to be rounding-safe.
Checkpoints, sources, main verification code and main verification report are not modified; only this separate audit artifact is created.
